reason: The registered recovery policy forbids execution while the provider-reported free-tier quota remains zero, but the initial recovery workflow relied on operator discipline rather than a machine-enforced pre-provider gate. This amendment closes that execution-control gap before any replacement call.
new_fail_closed_controls: Recovery checkout uses full history so frozen commits can be verified.
The trigger must bind the original recovery policy commit, primary workflow run, exact replacement-slot total, provider, model, temperature, instruction version and authority.
The workflow must verify the original recovery policy file has not drifted since its registered commit.
The workflow must reject execution before the provider-reported reset timestamp 2026-09-07T00:00:00Z.
The trigger must carry a recovery design commit; the workflow must fail before provider invocation if protected recovery dependencies drift between that commit and execution HEAD.
Only the trigger file may be added after the recovery design commit without invalidating the frozen recovery path.
interpretation: This amendment strengthens enforcement of the already-registered recovery policy. It does not authorize additional samples, change any model-visible input, replace a provider/model, alter temperature or instruction version, discard valid primary evidence, or change the scientific decision rule.
